Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:10:1.hebrew: דכ"ע חומש לא מעכב - שיהא האוכלו לוקה עליו משום "לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך" (שם יב):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:10:1.english: Everyone agrees [that] the one-fifth does not prevent [consumption] - [meaning] that one who eats it would incur lashes for it on account of "You may not eat within your gates" (ibid., 12).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:10:2.hebrew: והכא בחוששין לפשיעותא - הא דקאמר רבי יהושע לא יאכל, מדרבנן קאמר, שמא יפשע ויתיאש ולא יתן חומש עוד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:10:2.english: And here [they disagree] with regard to [whether] we are concerned for negligence - That which Rabbi Yehoshua said, "he may not eat," he said [as a] rabbinic [decree], lest he be negligent and give up [on paying], and not give [the] fifth anymore.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:11:1.hebrew: הואיל וגזברין תובעין אותו - את החומש, וליכא למיחש לפשיעותא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:11:1.english: Since the treasurers demand [from] him - the fifth, and there is no [reason] to be concerned about negligence.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:13:1.english: The statement of Rabbi Eliezer appears [correct] with regard to consecrated [property] - Since [the Temple] treasurers demand it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:15:1.hebrew: הרי אמרו - במסכת בכורות בפרק בתרא (ד' נא.):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:15:1.english: Behold, they said - In Tractate Bekhorot, in the last chapter (51a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:15:2.english: And he will give the money - [The verse states:] "And if the one who consecrated [it] redeems [his house], etc., he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be his."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:16:1.english: Terumah - A non-priest who eats it unwittingly.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:16:2.hebrew: אינה משתלמת - מעות, אלא פירות חולין, שהתשלומין נעשין תרומה, כדכתיב בו "את הקודש" — מה שהוא נותן לו נעשה קודש. אלמא, מידי דחזי להכי בעינן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:16:2.english: It is not repaid - [with] money, but rather [with] non-sacred produce, for the repayment becomes terumah, as it is written regarding it: "the sacred [thing]" — [meaning] that which he gives to him becomes sacred. Thus, we require something fit for this.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:16:3.hebrew: שלא מן החולין - מעות או בגדים, שוה כסף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:16:3.english: Not from non-sacred [produce] - Money or garments, [i.e.,] monetary equivalent.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:17:1.english: Upon it - In all [cases of the] fifths, it is written, "he shall add upon it."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:1.english: And did not eat it - For it is returned intact.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:2.english: He pays the double [payment] - of the theft fine in money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:3.hebrew: דמי תרומה - כמה שהיא שוה לימכר בשוק, ודמיה פחותין מדמי חולין; שאינה ראויה אלא לכהנים, ואינה ראויה בימי טומאתו, ואם מטמאה אסורה באכילה. לפיכך דמיה מועטים, והיינו דקאמר דמי תרומה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:3.english: The price of terumah - [According to] how much it is worth to be sold in the market, and its price is less than the price of non-sacred [produce]; for it is fit only for priests, and it is not fit [for a priest] during the days of his impurity, and if it becomes impure, it is forbidden for consumption. Therefore, its price is low, and this is what [the Mishnah] means when it says "the price of terumah."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:4.english: [If] he ate it - Unwittingly, as he did not know that it was terumah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:5.hebrew: שני קרנין - אחד לקרן ואחד לכפל, וחומש בשביל אכילתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:5.english: Two principals - One for the principal and one for the double [payment], and a fifth on account of eating it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:7.hebrew: והקרן - השני, שהוא בא מחמת כפל של קנס גניבה, משלם נמי דמי תרומה; כלומר, מעות כמו שנמכרת תרומה בשוק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:19:7.english: And the principal - The second [principal], which comes on account of the double [payment] of the theft fine, he likewise pays [at] the price of terumah — that is, money according to how terumah is sold in the market.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:1:1.hebrew: הבעלים נותנין - על כרחן עשרים ושש, שאי אפשר לתת לזה באחד ועשרים, שנמצא הקדש נפסד בחמשה סלעים, ולבעלים נמי לא פחתינן מן הקרן ששמאה איש אחר. הלכך, נותנין כ"א לקרן וחמשה לתוספת חומש, ועל עילויו של זה שהעלה בדמיו סלע אין מוסיף חומש, אלא על קרן ששמאה הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:1:1.english: The owners give - Perforce twenty-six [selas], for it is impossible to give [the consecrated item] to this [other person] for twenty-one, as [then] the Temple treasury would be found to lose five selas; and for the owners too, we do not reduce from the principal at which another man appraised it. Therefore, they give twenty-one for the principal and five for the addition of a fifth; and on the increment of this [other person] who raised its price by a sela, he does not add a fifth, [but] rather only on the principal at which he himself appraised it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:2:1.hebrew: עשרים וחמש הבעלים נותנין שלשים - והתם (ערכין ד' כז:) פריך: ונימא לגיזבר "אתא גברא בחריקאי" — הרי בא אחר תחתינו, שחפץ ליתן כמה שעולה קרן וחומש שאמרתי, ואין הקדש נפסד — ולמה נכוף את זה לתת שלשים? וסיום המשנה: "אמר אחד הרי הוא שלי בעשרים ושש, אומר הגעתיך":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:2:1.english: Twenty-five, the owner gives thirty - And there (Arakhin 27b), [the Gemara] asks: Let [the owner] say to the Temple treasurer, "Ata gavra bacharikai" — [meaning,] "Behold, another has come in our place, who wishes to give as much as the principal and fifth that I stated [would total], so the Temple treasury suffers no loss" — so why should we compel this [owner] to give thirty? And the conclusion of the Mishnah [reads]: "[If] one said, 'Behold, it is mine for twenty-six,' [the treasurer] says, 'It has reached you' [i.e., it is yours]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:2:2.hebrew: ש"מ חומשא מלבר - מדקתני חומש על עשרים סלעים חמש סלעים, הרי חומש מן החוץ:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:2:2.english: Learn from it [that] one-fifth [is calculated] from without - Since it teaches [that] the fifth on twenty selaim is five selaim, behold, [this is] a fifth from the outside.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:3:1.english: It and its fifth [total] five - That is, a fifth from without, which is a quarter of the principal.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:4:1.english: One-fifth prevents - [i.e., it prevents] eating [the produce] outside the wall [of Jerusalem] until he gives the fifth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:4:2.hebrew: אכנפשיה - מאיליו; אינו בכלל הפדיון, שארבעה הזוזים פדו מעשר שהוא כנגדם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:4:2.english: Upon himself - On his own; [the fifth] is not included in the redemption, for the four zuzim redeemed the [second] tithe that corresponds to them [in value].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:4:3.hebrew: או דלמא ארבעה בחמשה פריק - כך הוא גזירת הכתוב, שהחומש מן הפדיון הוא, ואין שוה ארבעה נפדין בפחות מחמשה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:4:3.english: Or perhaps four is redeemed with five - Such is the decree of Scripture, that the fifth is [part] of the redemption, and [items] worth four are not redeemed for less than five.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:5:1.english: The demai - [This refers to] the second tithe of demai [doubtfully tithed produce] that the Sages obligated one who buys from an am ha'aretz [an unlearned person] to separate.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:5:2.english: It has no [added] fifth - If its owner redeems it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:5:3.hebrew: ואין לו ביעור - בשנה שלישית, שנצטוו ישראל לבער כל מעשרותיהם מן הבית ולתת למי שהם רוצים, כדכתיב (דברים יד) מקצה שלש שנים וגו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:5:3.english: And there is no eradication for it - in the third year, when Israel was commanded to remove all their tithes from the house and give [them] to whomever they wish, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14[:28]): "At the end of three years, etc."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:6:1.hebrew: הא קרן יש לו - דכל זמן שלא פדאו, אסור לאוכלו חוץ לחומה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:6:1.english: But there is principal - For as long as one has not redeemed it, it is forbidden to eat it outside the wall [of Jerusalem].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:6:2.hebrew: מ"ט - אין לו חומש ויש לו קרן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:6:2.english: What is the reason - [That] it has no fifth, yet it has principal.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:6:3.english: Which prevents by Torah law - in [the case of] tithe [obligated] by Torah law.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:6:4.english: It is in rabbinic [law] - In [the case of] demai tithe, [which is] rabbinic.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:7:1.english: On Shabbat - Because of the honor of Shabbat, he should not be prevented from eating on account of [the] one-fifth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:8:1.hebrew: מדקאמר רבי נראין דברי ר' אליעזר בשבת - אבל בחול אינו רואה את דבריו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:8:1.english: From [the fact] that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says, "The words of Rabbi Eliezer appear [correct] on Shabbat" - However, on a weekday he does not view his words [as correct].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:8:2.hebrew: מכלל דאיהו אפילו בחול - אמר יאכל, ובמעשר ודאי קאמר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 54a:8:2.english: By inference, he [maintains that] even on a weekday - [Rabbi Eliezer] said one may eat [it], and he is speaking about definite tithe.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:15:1.hebrew: הקדש אינו מתחלל על הקרקע - הא דאמר שמואל לקמן (בבא מציעא דף נז:): "בונין בחול ואח"כ מקדישין", למ"ד (חולין דף טז.) תלוש ולבסוף חיברו הוי תלוש — אתי שפיר; ואפי' למ"ד חשוב כמחובר, מ"מ כיון דאם לא היה קדוש סופו ליעקר, מקרי תלוש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:15:1.english: Consecrated [property] cannot be desacralized with land - That which Shmuel says later (Bava Metzia 57b): "They build with unconsecrated [materials] and afterward consecrate [it]" — according to the one who says (Chullin 16a) [that something] detached and afterward attached [to the ground] is [considered] detached, it works out well; and even according to the one who says it is considered attached, nevertheless, since if it were not consecrated it would eventually be uprooted, it is called detached:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:15:2.hebrew: ונתן הכסף וקם לו - וא"ת: אי כסף דוקא, מטלטלין נמי לא; ואי גמרי' מנזקין ועבד, דכתיב בהן (שמות כא) "ישיב" לרבות שוה כסף ככסף, א"כ קרקע נמי! וי"ל: דדרשינן בכלל ופרט: "ויסף חמישית" — כלל, "כסף" — פרט, "והיה לו" — חזר וכלל. וכן משמע פ' יש בכור (בכורות ד' נא.), דתנן: "אין פודין את הבכור בקרקעות כו' ולא בהקדשות", ומפרש בגמ' "ולא הקדשות בכל אלו", והתם גבי בכור דריש בכלל ופרט וכלל. וא"ת: דאי לא הוה כתב אלא "כסף" לחודיה ה"א שוה כסף ככסף, והשתא דכתיבי כללי ממעטינן קרקעות? וי"ל: דהכא "כסף" מיותר, דה"מ למכתב "חמישית ערכך", וגבי בכור נמי "ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה בערכך ה' שקלים", ומדכתיב "כסף" — למדרשיה לפרטא הוא דאתא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:15:2.english: “And he will give the money and it will be assured to him” - And if you ask: If "money" [is meant] literally, [then] movable property should also not [be valid for redemption]; and if we derive [that movable property is valid] from [the laws of] damages and a [Hebrew] slave, regarding which it is written (Exodus 21) "he shall return," to include that which is worth money as [equivalent to] money, then land [should] also [be valid]! And one can answer: We expound [this verse] through a generalization and a specification: "And he shall add a fifth" — [this is] a generalization; "money" — [this is] a specification; "and it shall be his" — [this] generalizes again. And so it is implied in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 51a), where we learned in a Mishnah: "One may not redeem a firstborn with land, etc., nor with consecrated property," and it is explained in the Gemara: "nor [may one redeem] consecrated property with any of these," and there regarding a firstborn it expounds [the verse] through a generalization, a specification, and a generalization. And if you ask: If it had only written "money" by itself, I would have said that [all] money's worth is like money [including land], and now that generalizations are written, we exclude land?! And one can answer: Here, [the word] "money" is superfluous, for it could have written "a fifth of your valuation," and regarding a firstborn as well, [it could have written] "and its redemption from a month old shall you redeem according to your valuation, five shekels"; and since "money" is written, it comes [specifically] to be expounded as a specification.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:18:1.hebrew: עליו לרבות שחומשו כמותו - וא"ת: והלא אין חומש מעכב, א"כ אין חומש כמותו; ובסמוך גבי מעשר נמי אמרינן דאין מוסיף חומש על החומש? וי"ל, דעליו לא מיירי אלא בדבר שמשלם קרן, משלם חומש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:18:1.english: "Unto it," to include its one-fifth [as having the same status] as itself - And if you say: Is it not [the case that] the one-fifth is not essential [to the redemption], [and] if so, the one-fifth is not like itself; and just below regarding [second] tithe as well, we say that one does not add a fifth upon a fifth? And one can answer that "unto it" only speaks of [the rule that] in a matter where one pays the principal, one pays a fifth.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:19:1.hebrew: אף אנן נמי תנינא - ה"מ לאתויי מתני' דמייתי בסמוך, דמשלם חומשא דחומשא, וכיון שנעשה החומש תרומה, א"כ משתלם מדבר הראוי להיות קודש. ומיהו יש לדחות, דמצי לשלם בכל דבר, וכי משלם דבר הראוי להיות קודש — אז נעשה תרומה. אי נמי: מהך דהכא עדיפא ליה לאתויי, דקתני בהדיא "חומש מן החולין":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:19:1.english: We too learn - [Ravina] could have brought the Mishnah that [the Gemara] brings immediately afterward, which [states] that he pays a fifth of a fifth; and since the fifth becomes terumah, if so, it is paid from something fit to become sacred. However, [that proof] can be refuted, as he can pay with anything, and when he pays with something fit to become sacred — then it becomes terumah. Alternatively: it is preferable for him to bring [a proof] from this [Mishnah] here, because it teaches explicitly, "a fifth from non-sacred [items]."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:4:1.hebrew: או דלמא ד' בה' פריק וחומש מעכב - וא"ת: והלא בהקדש שוה מנה שחללו על שוה פרוטה מחולל, ומסתמא הוא הדין במעשר? וי"ל, דודאי אם אמר "הוא וחומשו מחולל על פרוטה" (פחות) מועיל, אבל כי לא מזכיר בהדיא החומש, לא מהני:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:4:1.english: Or perhaps four [dinars] are redeemed with five [dinars], and [failure to pay] the one-fifth prevents [consumption] - And if you ask: Is it not [the law] regarding consecrated property worth a maneh that if one redeemed it for [something] worth a perutah, it is redeemed, and presumably the same law applies to [second] tithe? One can answer that certainly if he said, "It and its one-fifth are redeemed for a perutah" (less), it is effective; however, when he does not explicitly mention the one-fifth, it is not effective.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:7:1.hebrew: אמר רבי נראין כו' - סבר חומש לא מעכב, ולכך בשבת חילל; אבל בחול לא חילל, דחיישינן לפשיעה, ובשבת לא חיישינן משום עונג:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 54a:7:1.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] said: [The statement of Rabbi Eliezer] appears, etc. - [He] holds [that] the one-fifth is not indispensable, and therefore on Shabbat he has deconsecrated [the produce]; however, on a weekday he has not deconsecrated [it], because we are concerned about negligence [in paying the one-fifth], whereas on Shabbat we are not concerned [about this] because of [Shabbat] enjoyment.
